visual_text: Two questions about the same stairs
Clinician: "Any difficulty with the stairs?" Patient: "No, I manage."
At home, she climbs one step at a time, both hands on the rail.
Clinician: "Have you changed how you do it, or how often?" Patient: "I only go up once a day now, and slowly."
Changing how you do a task, before any difficulty, was linked with later difficulty in more able women in their 70s in Baltimore (1990s studies).
Fried et al. 2000, 2001; Weiss et al. 2012
alt_text: Three-panel comic. A clinician asks a woman in her late 70s about difficulty with stairs and she says no. At home she climbs one step at a time holding the rail with both hands. The clinician then asks whether she has changed how or how often she climbs. Illustrative; linked to later difficulty in Baltimore studies.
